About the Position

A 4-year fully funded PhD programme training researchers in materials chemistry, digital intelligence, and automation, offering 10+ cross-disciplinary research projects.

OpportunityFully Funded EPSRC CDT in Digital & Automated Materials Chemistry (DAMC CDT)
HostUniversity of Liverpool
LocationLiverpool, United Kingdom
Study LevelPhD
FundingFully Funded
Stipend£21,805/year + £5,238 tuition fees covered
Application DeadlineOpen - Apply as soon as possible
ApplyOfficial application page ↗

Funding detail: £21,805 per year (maintenance grant) + £5,238 per year (fully covered tuition fees)

Basic Information

  • Full Programme Name: EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Digital and Automated Materials Chemistry
  • Host Institution: University of Liverpool
  • Funding Body: EPSRC (Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council)
  • Study Level: PhD
  • Duration: 4 years (48 months)
  • Start Date: October 2026
  • Number of Projects: 10+ cross-disciplinary research projects
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded
  • Stipend: £21,805 (2026/27 UKRI minimum) per year (maintenance grant)
  • Tuition Fees: £5,238 per year (fully covered)
  • Eligibility: Open to home and international students
  • Application Deadline: Open until filled (apply as soon as possible)

About the Programme

The DAMC CDT trains cohorts of researchers with capabilities in materials chemistry, digital intelligence, and automation. Students develop core expertise in robotic, digital, chemical, and physical thinking, which they apply in domain-specific research in materials design, discovery, and processing. The programme includes a tailored training programme to develop both technical and leadership skills.

Research Focus

  • Materials chemistry
  • Digital intelligence and automation
  • Robotic and automated experimentation
  • AI-driven materials discovery
  • Sustainable materials design

Programme Structure

  • 4-year integrated PhD
  • Tailored training programme
  • Cross-disciplinary research projects
  • Industry engagement and collaboration

Available Projects (2026-27)

  1. A Fast Validation of the Symmetry Principle for Molecular Synthesisability
  2. Automated Virtual and Physical Screening of Molecules for Application in Optoelectronics Devices
  3. Autonomous, On-Demand Manufacture of Polymer Nanomaterials in Continuous-Flow
  4. Crystal Structure Generation by Constrained Combinatorial Sampling
  5. Digital Exploration of Novel Polymeric Materials for Structural Composites
  6. Digital Exploration of Sulfur-Polymer Development
  7. Discovering CO2-capture materials using robots and 'Hive Mind' hybrid intelligence
  8. Discovering Design Rules in Product Formulation using Automated Rheo-Dialysis and Scattering
  9. Discovering New Materials in the Laboratory with Automated Reasoning and Explainable AI
  10. Introducing Temperature and Disorder into Digital Materials Discovery Workflows
  11. Mitigating Synthesisability Loss in 3D Generative Models
  12. Putting a (Better) Brain in the Mobile Robotic Chemist
  13. Real Time Mixing Control in Flow Chemistry

Eligibility and Requirements

  • First Class or 2:1 Honours degree in chemistry, materials science, chemical engineering, or related discipline
  • Relevant Master's degree preferred
  • International students welcome
  • IELTS 6.5 (minimum) for non-native English speakers

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/doctoral-training/digital-and-automated-materials-chemistry/prospective-students/how-to-apply/

Source: liverpool.ac.uk - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Open - Apply as soon as possible - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Apply via the University of Liverpool's postgraduate research portal. Select DAMC CDT and choose your preferred project.

Application guides

  • How to Read a PhD Job Advert: Funding, Eligibility and Application Steps
  • Academic CV for PhD Applications: Structure and an Example
  • UK Student Visa Application: CAS, Documents and Financial Evidence
